alt: Amazon Kindle 2026 e-reader showing its redesigned flush-glass front and the new removable back panel added for EU right-to-repair battery-replacement compliance — the same panel that testers found pops off accidentally when the device is removed from a tight case
story: Amazon's 2026 Kindle redesign added a removable back panel to comply with EU right-to-repair battery-replacement rules; Mashable testing found the panel pops off when the device is pulled from a tight case — Amazon's official response: 'If the back panel accidentally comes off, it does not mean the device is broken; just press it firmly back into place at all four corners.'
why_funny: Amazon made the Kindle 'repair-friendly' by designing a back that detaches for battery swaps — but it also detaches when you take it out of a case, so the fix for the EU repair mandate is now its own repair problem.
